title: Locally zero sections detect maps from a presheaf with zero sheafification on a finite basis
statement: Let (C,J) be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], A a Grothendieck abelian coefficient category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and B a predicate on objects of C. Assume finite products in every Over V and that each covering sieve of a B-object contains a finite covering family all of whose nonempty repeated nerve terms satisfy B. Let P:C^op→A have zero sheafification. For V satisfying B and b:P(V)→T, suppose that for each such finite basis cover U of V, every coefficient object E and x:E→P(V), vanishing of all restrictions of x to the one-fold nerve terms of U implies x≫b=0. Then b=0. Different locally zero generalized sections may use different finite covers.

source.place: Section 7.10, the filtered-colimit local equality description before Lemma 7.10.8 and the finite-composition argument of Theorem 7.10.10 (Tag 00WB); categorical extension using AB5 and transfinite plus, not a claim of verbatim coefficient generality.

proof.text: For each covering sieve form the kernel of restriction from P(V) to its matching-family object. Refinement gives a filtered family. AB5 identifies its union with the kernel of the plus unit, since plus is the filtered colimit of matching-family objects. Refining the sieve to a finite B-cover shows that each such kernel is killed by a finite restriction map.

Iterate plus transfinitely, using the source library TransfinitePlus and TransfinitePlusSheaf constructions. At a successor step pull back local kernels along the earlier unit. Inductively express the restrictions on each of finitely many covering members as filtered unions of further local kernels. Commute these unions with finite pullbacks and products by AB5, compose the finite covers, and refine again by the given basis hypothesis. Before invoking hcov on a covering member, replace the family by its canonically isomorphic one-fold nerve family, whose members satisfy B literally. Refining the final composite at V restores the stipulated nerve condition. No invariance of B under isomorphism is assumed. Thus the pulled-back kernel is a union of kernels killed on finite B-covers.

At a limit ordinal AB5 identifies the kernel with the union of earlier kernels. For a sufficiently large regular cardinal the transfinite plus construction is a sheafification. Its value is zero by the hypothesis and uniqueness of sheafification, so the union of locally zero kernels is all of P(V). The hypothesis on b kills each kernel, and hence b.

lean.statement:
theorem hom_eq_zero_of_sheafification_zero
    (B : C → Prop)
    (hcov : ∀ V, B V → ∀ R ∈ J V, ∃ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → Over V),
      (∀ (k : ℕ) (y : Fin (k + 1) → Fin n), B (Presheaf.cechNerveObj U y).left) ∧
      (∀ a, R (U a).hom) ∧
      Sieve.ofArrows (fun a ↦ (U a).left) (fun a ↦ (U a).hom) ∈ J V)
    (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A) (hP : IsZero ((presheafToSheaf J A).obj P))
    (V : C) (hV : B V) {T : A} (b : P.obj (op V) ⟶ T)
    (h : ∀ {n : ℕ} (U : Fin n → Over V),
      (∀ (k : ℕ) (y : Fin (k + 1) → Fin n), B (Presheaf.cechNerveObj U y).left) →
      Sieve.ofArrows (fun a ↦ (U a).left) (fun a ↦ (U a).hom) ∈ J V →
      ∀ {E : A} (x : E ⟶ P.obj (op V)),
        x ≫ cechAugmentation U Over.mkIdTerminal ((Over.forget V).op ⋙ P) = 0 →
        x ≫ b = 0) : b = 0
